**Overview**

We’re adding a new “Admin” page that lets **you** (the site owner) see every customer’s orders.  
Because you’ll be looking at private customer data, this feature is **Amber** – it requires log‑in, personal data protection, and safe defaults for the backend.

Below is a one‑screen plan that includes the safety parts we’ll build, a quick list of what we need from you, and the first step to get started.

---

### One‑screen plan

```
What we are building
 • A protected Admin page that lists all customer orders.

Who uses it
  • You (the site owner).  Risk level: Amber (log‑in + private customer data).

Day‑one features
  1. Login page for you (magic‑link email).
  2. Admin page that fetches and displays every order.
  3. Simple “sign out” button.

Information it stores
  • Supabase tables: `orders` + `users` (public data is already in place).
  • No new private data – just read access to existing tables.

Logins
  • Use Supabase Auth (magic link login).  This gives a secure, email‑only login flow.
  • The admin page will require the user to be authenticated **AND** have an `is_admin` claim.

Money
  • None – just data reading.

Built with
  • Lovable for hosting + live preview.
  • Supabase (Postgres) for data and auth.
  • SSR page for the admin (so the data never hits the browser).

Safety items we’ll add
  • **Login – magic link** (no password).  
  • **`is_admin` flag** on the logged‑in session; only you can set it (manual in Supabase).  
  • **Row‑level security (RLS)**: `orders` table will have a policy that allows only `is_admin` to read all rows.  
  • **Secret key** (Supabase service_role) stays in the server side (Lovable build Env).  
  • **Save points** before each code change; you can restore if something breaks.
  • **Ship‑check**: after we finish, run the built‑in Lovable scan to audit for exposed secrets.
```

**Does this look correct?**  
Reply `yes` or tell me what to change. If you’re happy, I’ll give you the exact code snippets to paste into your Lovable project and the next small step (adding the `is_admin` flag and policy).
